AC Repair in Spring, Texas, a Community Without a City Hall

Spring is a name on thousands of mailing addresses but not a city, so there is no city permit office and no city utility. The free line answers 24 hours a day and hands your call to a locally owned HVAC business serving Spring.

If you need AC repair in Spring, Texas, you are in a large, busy community that has never been a city. That shapes who you call for what: there is no city utility, no city inspector and no city hall. This page sorts out who does what for Spring heating and cooling, and what the free call involves.

Houston Air & Heating fixes nothing on its own. Dialing (832) 662-4107 gets you an automated assistant that notes heat or cooling and the symptom, then puts you through to a Spring-area HVAC business owned by local people. Diagnosis, quote, repair and the bill all come from that business.

Spring: a railroad town that became a suburb

Spring grew up around a railroad that opened through the area in 1871. After the railroad moved its roundhouse to Houston in 1923, the town shrank to around 300 people by 1931. In the 1970s some of the old houses in the original town, now Old Town Spring off Spring Cypress Road, were restored and reopened as shops, and the Old Town Spring Association followed in 1980.

Today the Spring census designated place counted 62,559 people in 2020, and the Spring name stretches across a large part of northern Harris County and a small piece of Montgomery County. Because of that sprawl, a Spring address can mean a small older cottage near the historic district, a 1980s ranch home or a brand new two-story in a master planned community, each with very different equipment.

Unincorporated Spring: who handles what

Without a city, the jobs a city hall would do are split up. This is how it sorts out for a heating and cooling problem.

The HVAC company

Diagnoses, prices and repairs or replaces your system. Texas requires it to hold an Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractor license from TDLR whether or not you live in a city.

Your electric bill

Names the company that delivers your power and restores outages. If the house is dark, report it there. Power on but no cooling points to your equipment, which is HVAC business, not utility business.

Your HOA

If your subdivision has deed restrictions and a replacement moves the outdoor unit or adds equipment, check whether the association wants to approve it first.

What usually fails in a Spring home, by age

Common cooling issues in Spring homes by age of house
Type of homeWhat to ask about
Older homes near the historic districtSmall closets and tight crawl or attic space for equipment, and whether the ducts were ever resized after additions.
1980s and 1990s subdivisionsSystems on their second or third replacement, older refrigerant types, and ductwork that has sagged or pulled loose in the attic.
Newer master planned communitiesTwo systems in a two-story house, an upstairs unit that works harder in the attic heat, and warranty paperwork on fairly young equipment.

This is a general pattern, not a diagnosis. Remodels and past replacements change everything, so the technician's own inspection of your equipment is what counts.

When it quits at 2 a.m.

A lot of people searching for 24 hour AC repair in Spring are sitting in a warm house in the middle of the night. A few safe checks can save a call or help the technician later:

  1. Thermostat: Cool mode, a number lower than the current indoor reading, and new batteries in models that take them.
  2. Filter: a filter caked with dust can choke airflow until the indoor coil ices over. Replace it if it is dirty.
  3. Breaker: one reset is fine. A repeat trip is a signal to stop and phone.
  4. Water: look for water around the indoor unit. Some systems shut themselves off when the drain backs up.

Anything beyond those checks, including refrigerant, wiring and parts inside the cabinets, belongs to a technician. Large storms such as Hurricane Beryl in July 2024, which left hundreds of thousands of Houston-area customers still without power five days later, are a reminder to know where your breaker panel is and how your thermostat works before you need to.

Help the company find you

Because "Spring" covers so much ground, the name alone tells a company very little about where you are. Two homes with Spring addresses can sit far apart, on opposite sides of a freeway or even in different counties. When you call, be ready with details that save time on both ends:

  • Your ZIP code and nearest major cross streets, not just "Spring."
  • The subdivision name, plus any gate code or guard desk instructions the technician will need.
  • Where the equipment lives: attic, garage closet or hallway closet for the indoor unit, and which side of the house the outdoor unit is on.
  • How many systems the house has, and which floor or rooms are affected.
  • What it is doing: blowing warm air, running nonstop, icing, leaking, buzzing or completely dead.

Those few facts help the business you are connected with decide whom to send and what parts may be needed, and they make the first visit more useful.

Heating repair in Spring when the weather turns

The first cold mornings of fall bring calls about furnaces that will not light and heat pumps blowing cool air. Check the thermostat is on Heat, the filter is clean and the breaker has not tripped. Should a gas furnace ever leave an odor of gas in the house, step outdoors and phone the gas utility listed on your statement, or 911. Carbon monoxide alarms call for the same exit first, then 911.

Services Spring homes ask about most

Start with AC repair for warm air, ice or a unit that will not start. If it is the middle of the night or the house is getting dangerously hot, read emergency AC repair. For an older system that keeps failing, repair or replace walks through the decision, and heating repair covers furnaces and heat pumps.

Verify the license before work begins. Texas requires anyone contracting to do air conditioning, refrigeration or heating work to hold an Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (ACR) Contractor license from the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR). Ask the company for its ACR license number, then confirm it on the TDLR license search (opens in a new tab). The line does not check this for you.

Common questions

Where can I find 24 hour AC repair in Spring, TX?

The phone line itself never closes: an automated assistant picks up around the clock and connects you with a Spring-area heating and cooling business. How soon a technician can arrive is up to that business and how busy the night is, so ask once you are talking. When no one answers on their end, the assistant keeps your name and number so the company can ring you back.

Is Spring, Texas a city?

No. Spring is an unincorporated community in Harris County, counted by the Census Bureau as a census designated place, and the Spring name also covers a small part of southern Montgomery County. There is no Spring city government, so there is no city building department.

Spring has no city hall, so is a permit needed for a new AC?

There is no Spring city permit office, but that does not mean anything goes. Texas still requires the company to hold an ACR contractor license from TDLR, and your homeowners association may have rules about outdoor equipment. Ask the company what approvals apply to your address and get the answer on the quote.

Who handles heating repair in Spring, TX?

The same free line. Mention heat, and the assistant routes you to a heating business working the Spring area. Gas odor in the house? Walk outside before you phone the gas utility or 911. A carbon monoxide detector going off means the same: everyone out, then 911.

Spring AC or heat out? Call the free line any hour

One free call, any hour. Say whether it is the AC or the heat, where you are and what is happening, and the line transfers you to an independent, locally owned HVAC company that looks at the system and prices the job itself.
